summary: Proceed with no companion: the change is a single swapped kernel behind a per-class gate, so the profile row (_silu_mul_local_kernel vs act_and_mul_kernel 1.8-5.7 us) and the [silu2] print line make one run interpretable on their own. Its expected value is low, though, and the gate as specified (warm-L2 bare-kernel replay) is the step most likely to mislead. The one prior Triton replacement of act_and_mul in this repo (prefill silu-mul-triton-local-rows-marlin-turn) ran 2x SLOWER on the judge (14.2 -> 29.4 us, 52.9 -> 86.0 us), so make the gate time it the way the judge does.
justification: Numbers check out: master's submit profile 7a0d900a1dd34666 (archive/w2-marlin-atomic-add-small-m) has act_and_mul_kernel at 1.8/2.1/2.4/2.2/3.7/5.7 us for bs 1/16/32/8/128/256, and a2744bc496b84790 repeats them within 0.1-0.3 us (1.5/2.2/2.4/2.0/4.0/5.6), so the kernel row can be read to well under the claimed deltas. The mechanism is plausible only at the verify shapes. At bs=256, T*8 = 2048 one-row CTAs is a real scheduling cost. The local gate+up rows (skewed routing makes this GPU the busiest, so plausibly 3/8 or more of the routes are local, about 12-16 MB) were just written by the w13 Marlin and can sit in the 50 MB L2. 5.7 -> ~3 us is therefore reachable but not guaranteed. At bs <= 32, 1.8-2.4 us is mostly launch and tail latency, and a Triton launch is no cheaper, so 'flat' (gate keeps master) is the honest expectation and the hypothesis says so. The expected shapes match TASK.md: every load weighs 60, the deltas are about 0.4-0.5% per touched row (below the +-1.5% headline CI), and the hypothesis tells the reader to judge on the kernel row, which is right. WEAKEST LINK: the go/no-go rests on a warm-L2, bare-kernel, 41-replay graph microbenchmark of a ~2-6 us kernel. (a) Per-replay event timing of one ~2 us kernel with an empty-graph baseline subtracted is close to the timer's resolution, so a 1.05x threshold can be crossed by noise. (b) Warm replay keeps cache1 AND cache2 in L2 and leaves out the w13 Marlin's eviction pressure: it streams up to ~512 MB of NVFP4 w13 weights through L2 right before silu, so 'just written, therefore resident' is an assumption. (c) Repo precedent: prefill's silu-mul-triton-local-rows-marlin-turn (archive b2259479e57e4196) was reviewed with an expected 14.2 -> ~5-6 us and measured 29.4 us on the judge (2x slower). That differs in kind (a sorted-id gather, BLOCK_R 16 x 512 at 4 warps), but it shows SGLang's act_and_mul is not an easy target for a 2-D tiled Triton elementwise kernel. Sharp note for the builder: time the gate in a graph that contains the w13 Marlin followed by silu (candidate vs silu_and_mul), with an L2-flush buffer read before each replay as the judge does, and subtract a w13-only graph. Or at least put K=20 back-to-back silu launches in each replayed graph and divide, so that per-launch timer noise does not decide the 1.05x gate. Second note: the hypothesis does not mention the prefill regression. It should be added to the risk text so a slower row is read as the known failure mode and not as the warm-L2 caveat alone.
confounders: w2-marlin-atomic-add-small-m: cache3 aliases cache13, so w2's output overwrites cache1's storage after silu. Ordering on one stream makes this safe, but _silu2_setup's end-to-end check must call _forward with state['w2_mode'] (the mode actually shipped at T<=32), not 'master', or the check does not cover the path that runs. The atomic mode does not change silu's own time, so it does not confound the kernel row.

triton-map-align-on-block-m-restack / align-parallel-per-expert-verify: these produce local_ids, which the new kernel uses as its validity mask (ids >= 0). SGLang's act_and_mul consumes the same tensor today, so the -1 contract is already exercised, and neither confounds the timing. The Triton kernel indexes rows by route slot, not sorted_ids, so the block_size_m pick (marlin-block-m-two-smaller-on-postnorm) does not touch it at all.

Not landed but relevant to value: BEST.json (1.3727x) is the unpromoted wgmma rewrite cuda-nvfp4-wgmma-rega-grouped-s5-copy-safe-bucket-gate. Its submission_blob field reads 60dfe35d, which is master's Marlin-only blob, so the record looks mislabeled. That rewrite fuses silu into its w13 at 128<=T<=512, so the only shapes this hypothesis expects to move (t128, t256) are the ones the rewrite line would make dead code. On master's 1.3445x lineage, a scored submit of this change will land near 1.345-1.35, below the board best, and will not move the board.
interference: No companion. Both a gain and a loss can be read without one. The profile replaces the act_and_mul_kernel row with _silu_mul_local_kernel at the same shapes, between the same Marlin producer and consumer. The [silu2] PATH CHOSEN line says per class whether the gate enabled it, with the gate's own sgl/triton microbench numbers to compare against the judge row. Classes the gate leaves on master are an in-run control for drift. No landed hypothesis changes what silu reads or how long it takes (see confounders), so an ab-revert would measure nothing new. A control that isolates a sub-change has nothing to isolate either, because there is only one kernel. Since every extra run is a scored submit today, a companion is clearly not worth it. If the judge row comes out slower than act_and_mul, the follow-up is a stacked hypothesis that changes the gate's timing method or turns the class off, not an A/B.
rules_flags: JIT in the timed path: Triton specializes integer args on divisibility by 16. n_rows = T*8 is a multiple of 16 for even T but not for odd T (bs=1 -> 8, the bs=33 test -> 264, the bs=257 test -> 2056). The representative T set (1, 8, 16, 32, 128, 256) therefore does not pre-compile the variants that the bs=33/257 tests hit, which contradicts 'nothing JIT-compiles in kernel_fn'. Use @triton.jit(do_not_specialize=['n_rows']) as the prefill _silu_mul_sorted_kernel does, and make I a constexpr (4096), or compile both specializations per enabled class in prepare().

Precision is OK as specified: fp32 silu(gate)*up with one bf16 round matches SGLang, activations stay BF16, and the weights are untouched. Masked loads and stores keep the uninitialised remote rows of cache1/cache2 out of the math, which is correct because the w2 Marlin reads only rows named in sorted_ids (padding sentinels are out of range).

Nothing derived from inputs is cached: the gate is decided once in prepare() on synthetic routings and keyed only by shape class, a host branch on num_tokens. state['silu2'] holds plain ints. There is no host sync in _forward. The microbench and e2e checks run untimed, well inside the 300 s prepare budget.

The gate's 1-ulp per-element bound against act_and_mul may reject a correct kernel, because tl.exp lowers to ex2.approx with a log2e multiply, which can differ from __expf/expf by a ulp in fp32 and occasionally flip a bf16 rounding. This cannot break a rule (a rejected class falls back to master), but if every class prints 'master' with max ulp 2, the run measured master. Treat the rel-L2 <= 1e-3 and e2e 5e-3 bounds as the real correctness gate.
open_questions: What fraction of the T*8 route rows is local under the judge's skewed routing at bs=128/256? The 'most CTAs exit immediately' premise and the 12-16 MB L2-residency estimate both depend on it. The gate could print the local-row count of its skewed synthetic case for comparison.

Why was prefill's Triton silu 2x slower than act_and_mul (gather through sorted_ids, 4 warps x 16x512 tile, or cold-L2 behaviour)? If the cause was cold L2 rather than the gather, the warm-L2 gate here will pass candidates that lose on the judge.

Is a scored submit worth it for a <=0.5%-per-row change on master's 1.3445x lineage, when the board best (1.3727x) comes from the unlanded wgmma rewrite that already replaces silu at 128<=T<=512? If the wgmma line is promoted, only the decode classes of this change survive, and they are expected to stay flat.

BEST.json records submission_blob 60dfe35d (master's Marlin-only file) for the wgmma s5 job 4e4a0e26c85944f2. Is the churn index writing the wrong blob, and does that mislead promotion or base selection?
